name: hook
text: Six unknown currents in one network. Two rules are enough to find them all.

name: build
text: So start smaller. A twelve volt battery drives current through a four ohm resistor, then the path splits into a twelve ohm and a six ohm branch, and rejoins at node B.

name: kcl
text: That split is the first rule. At any node, the current arriving equals the current leaving. Here, one and a half amps arrive, and half an amp plus one amp leave. Nothing is lost at the junction.

name: kcl_why
text: And this is not a coincidence. Charge cannot pile up at a point. If more arrived than left, it would accumulate, and the circuit would not be steady. This is conservation of charge.

name: kvl
text: Now the second rule. Pick any closed loop and walk it. Cross the battery and the potential rises twelve volts. Cross the resistors and it drops: six volts, then six more. The changes sum to zero.

name: kvl_why
text: You walked back to where you started, so you had to end at the same potential. Every volt gained was spent. That is conservation of energy.

name: resolve
text: So these are not formulas to memorise. Current sums to zero at a node because charge is conserved. Voltage sums to zero around a loop because energy is conserved.
